convoLines.text: "Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast."
"There's still the matter of the ambush of Sarah. Nobody's settled it."
Done — their story has a crack in it now.
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
"And... scene. Good talk."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything. Makes sense to me."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
Counted.
"Still on whether you're angry."
"Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? You doing okay?"
"Since Sophia died... I keep expecting to see Sophia at the fire. Stupid."
You show them Blackberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I tend the fire without being asked. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I asked Sophia about the talking-to-strangers part — Sophia's gone. ...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
They pull back half a step — not leaving, just... further.
"Still on the talking-to-strangers part. I've said enough."
"It gave us a codex. You know what that tells me? It expects us to need one. Plan accordingly."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"I should get back to it."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the east treeline."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the east treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Sophia always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Blackberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I asked Jad about the pantry run — Jad's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"There's still the matter of the ambush of you. Nobody's settled it."
"Nothing to show. Just my word."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
The ground remembers.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"Right. Well." That's the whole goodbye.

"Jad and I never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 5 days back. You're wearing Jad's shoes now — want to pick it up? 'A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.'"
"There's still the matter of the ambush of you. Nobody's settled it."
"Nothing to show. Just my word."
Names, named.
You follow the food, the gifts, the sudden friendliness. Nothing you can prove — yet. Dig again; the trail is still warm.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
Counted.
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"I could talk all day, but — go on. We'll talk more."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.

lines: d6: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d6: 🕯️ Sophia Ortiz is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d6: What Sophia kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d6: Jad picks up the journal. Their hands shake. Then they open it, and keep writing.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Tireless Stride (Level 1). You walk like water downhill — no wasted steps, no wasted breath. Every mile costs 15% less.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Weather (Level 1). Red sky at night, shepherd's delight. Red sky at morning, shepherd's warning. It works.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Star Navigation (Level 1). North Star is constant. Find the Big Dipper, follow the pointer stars. You always know north.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.
d6: 📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 1). Fear is data, not orders. Acknowledge it, then decide anyway. Courage is fear that kept going.
d6: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d6: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Sophia Ortiz, 6 days. The mantle passes to Jad Rizk.
d6: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Jad Rizk, 28 — a bush pilot. Their hands know different work now: Night Eyes.
d6: The fire knew Jad — solid ground, earned at this fire.

d11: 📖 LEARNED: Welding & Metalwork (Level 1). Join metal with heat: clean the joint, mind the arc, let it cool slow.
d11: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d11: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d11: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
